title: Removal of $2 Minimum for Charity Deductions
body:
Deal: Removal of $2 Minimum for Charity Deductions

[jsb] Thanks. I will hold onto my 1c until I hear from you next FY
[HopSkipJumpFallSplat] 1c says you'll forget to report back next FY :-)
[Benoffie] I understand that the ATO probably think that, due to electronic lodgements, this won't add a huge burden. But this minute claims crp has got to stop.
People will see it as a win for charity and the little guy. I just wish we'd outright stop returns for refund amounts under $500/$1000. Useless.
[Tacooo] I just wish we'd outright stop returns for refund amounts under $500/$1000. Useless.
Are you saying people who are owed a refund under $500/$1000 shouldn't get it or am I misreading this?
[Benoffie] Yeah can them. But I also think the tax free threshold should go up.
But that's another discussion.
Tax returns for such little money when the government has all your records is now pointless. Equally, lodgement to advise no income - get rid of that also.
ATO just looooves keeping itself busy….
[Tacooo] So hard working Aussies should just what? Let the government keep even more of their hard earned money? You've got to be kidding me.
Tax returns for such little money when the government has all your records is now pointless.
Tell that to the people who rely on a little cash injection right about now. What's more pointless is the ATO requiring you to file when you've got such a little refund expected instead of just paying out their calculated amount (that they already know).
[Benoffie] @Tacooo: You've completely missed the point.
If the tax free threshold moved from the current $18200 to even a minor $20000, you've already gained $1800.
Why should the system then bother about $50 refunds or give out $250 pork barrelling payments?
Henry actually recommended the threshold move to $25000.
Call me silly but I'd rather an extra $6800 tax free pa and no refund than whatever BS amount Ive been getting.
https://treasury.gov.au/review/the-australias-future-tax-sys…
[Big L] @Benoffie: He probably sold it the same way that you just have, that's why we continue the farce.
It's not the ATO keeping themselves in a job, it's treasury and finance advising government, and those governments trying to stay in power.
We get what we deserve.
[Benoffie] A government ideally should balance:
cost of compliance and administration
tax collected
tax returned
The ATO is too heavy. It employs around 20,000 people, consumes about $4-5b pa. Whilst it makes huge amounts ($600b pa), that doesnt make our tax system efficient.
We shouldn't be encouraging or forcing people to continuously have to engage with the tax system simply to gain their entitled incomes. That's stupid.
It's much more efficient to increase GST, reduce brackets, increase the threshold and remove duplication. Those recommendations are 20? years old now
[Big L] How about just getting company tax to z reasonable portion of the tax intake?
[mk8] I mean, $10 should probably be a basis, but $500, c'mon. How many people can afford $500-1000 as a donation to charity running/whatever events?
[Benoffie] A person who donates $500 would, hopefully, gain a receipt.
I doubt they would be under the tax free threshold or even under the 19% current bracket.
If changes were made and a $500 min limit set, they could add other receipts over $500 and lodge, receiving the x amount refund relevant to their tax bracket (say, 37% back)
But why should or would any sane agency encourage tax claims of less than $2? It's ridiculous
[nokidsandthreemoney] Far out, I can't wait to vote out this insanely incompetent government. If they honestly think this is some sort of win for the Australian people, it just further demonstrates how misaligned their priorities are with the real world.
[nokidsandthreemoney] Respectfully, I think we as a population are far too calm. We don't make enough fuss when a government becomes tyrannical and begins to strip away our rights and abruptly alter policies without even so much as consultation. I know no party is perfect, but this one is currently faaaaar from even mediocre.
[Fuzor] Albaneseeee is pretty much the worst leader in this country's history. If only Trump is willing to rule Australia and get rid of this federal government
[shortgum] ls this another labour box of tricks to flight inflation? or show inter generation support for first home buyer into housing market?
[pharcyde] The latter. Also pillaging mum and dad's share portfolio's will somehow help Jaxxon and Mikayla-Ann-Rose-Lee buy their first $1.2m hoom with only $30k down!
[Big L] How is M&Ds share portfolio being pillaged?!
[roddy84] This post isn't exactly correct and ATO allows donations up to a total of $10 total without invoices if some light conditions are met.
So if your total is $10 or under receipts are probably not needed.
[metalslaw] if it's like any other dollar amount on a tax return, the amount will be truncated/stripped of cents, and thus rounded down to nearest whole dollar, lol.
